name: Johanan
overview: Johanan was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted as the sixth-born son of Meshelemiah (also known as Shallum). His identity is primarily grounded in his lineage within the Levitical family, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:3. There are no additional biographical details or notes beyond his tribal affiliation and birth order.
namesAndTitles: The name Johanan means 'YHWH has been gracious,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in God's graciousness. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation consistent with Levitical heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Johanan as the son of Shallum, also referred to as Meshelemiah, establishing his place within a Levitical family line. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Johanan's significance in Scripture lies chiefly in his role as a Levitical descendant, contributing to the genealogical record that underscores the continuity of God's chosen priestly tribe. His identification as the sixth son of Meshelemiah situates him within the broader context of temple service and Levitical duties, highlighting the faithfulness of God's covenant people through successive generations.
